title: DEFLATE compressed data format (RFC 1951)
summary: DEFLATE is the core compression algorithm used by gzip, zlib, and ZIP. It combines LZ77 (sliding window, 32KB) with Huffman coding. The bitstream consists of blocks: each block has a 3-bit header (BFINAL, BTYPE) followed by either stored data, fixed Huffman codes, or dynamic Huffman codes with a code-length alphabet.

ext.summary: DEFLATE is the core compression algorithm used by gzip, zlib, and ZIP. It combines LZ77 (sliding window, 32KB) with Huffman coding. The bitstream consists of blocks: each block has a 3-bit header (BFINAL, BTYPE) followed by either stored data, fixed Huffman codes, or dynamic Huffman codes with a code-length alphabet.

structure.meaning: 1 if this is the last block.
00 = stored (uncompressed), 01 = fixed Huffman, 10 = dynamic Huffman, 11 = reserved (error).
If BTYPE=00: LEN (2 bytes) + NLEN (2 bytes, one's complement) + LEN bytes of literal data.
If BTYPE=01: literals 0-143 = 8 bits, 144-255 = 9 bits, 256-279 = 7 bits, 280-287 = 8 bits; distances 0-31 = 5 bits.

If BTYPE=10: code length counts (5 bits each for 286 lit/len + 30 dist codes), then code lengths for the code-length alphabet, then the actual lit/len and distance code lengths, then the compressed data.
A back-reference: <length (3-258), distance (1-32768)> encoded as (length code, extra bits) + (distance code, extra bits).

ext.example_decoded: Minimal empty DEFLATE stream (BFINAL=1, BTYPE=00 stored, LEN=0)
notes: Huffman codes are canonical: shorter codes for more frequent symbols.
Distance codes 0-29 map to distances 1-32768 with extra bits for larger ranges.
DEFLATE is used by gzip, zlib, ZIP, PNG (IDAT), PDF, and many others.
